readme: FLOW-13's reason-code table, emitted by tools/gen-codes-table.mjs from the two files in `codes_source` and from nothing else.

This file is an INTERMEDIATE and not the published interface. The published one is FLOW-13's table inside SCOPE-7's `schema/contract-tokens-v1.json`, where astra-plugins-ops `tools/contract-tokens.mjs --codes <this file>` merges it (0.13.0's n8).

`codes` is the complete list of every code name those sources define. It is here so the merge can compare the table with the population in BOTH directions: without it a deleted row is indistinguishable from a code that does not exist, which was watched, and passed.
`codes_owed` names the B.7 codes this table cannot carry yet and who owes their title and remedy. An absent code is recorded, never silently dropped.
`codes_absent` names the B.7 codes that have no row because the contract gives them none: the waits the bot reports, which FLOW-10 renders from the result and not from this table.

codes_owed.owed_by: the contract sentence each code's reason names
codes_owed.why: FLOW-13 requires one full entry per reason code, and `fix` is a closed list naming what clears the code. For an owed code the contract states no `fix`, so a row here would be this repository's answer to a contract question.

codes_absent.why: B.7: FLOW-13's table lists "the codes … and the waits only the service shows". Each of these is a wait the bot reports, in a result's `wait` or by answering with no record (FLOW-72). FLOW-10 shows every wait by its start, cause and earliest retry, never from the table. So none of them carries a row, and each is recorded here so that it does not read as dropped.

each.W_LEASE_EXPIRED: FLOW-10 renders it; B.7 gives the table only service-only waits
each.W_ELIGIBILITY_UNREADABLE: FLOW-10 renders it; B.7 gives the table only service-only waits
each.W_NOTICE_PENDING: FLOW-10 renders it; B.7 gives the table only service-only waits
each.W_GITHUB_RATE_LIMITED: FLOW-10 renders it; B.7 gives the table only service-only waits
each.W_SERVICE_UNREACHABLE: FLOW-10 renders it; B.7 gives the table only service-only waits
each.W_MODERATION_HOLD: FLOW-10 renders it; B.7 gives the table only service-only waits
each.W_ALERT_UNDELIVERED: FLOW-10 renders it; B.7 gives the table only service-only waits
each.W_OPERATOR_WINDOW: FLOW-10 renders it; B.7 gives the table only service-only waits

flow13_table.title: Binding revoked by its bound account
flow13_table.remedy: The listing's bound account revoked its binding token from the Astra plugins panel (ID-17). Nothing needs clearing. From the next verdict a release still carrying the old line is refused `B_BINDING_UNUSABLE`, and one carrying a fresh token's line is held for a moderator as a changed binding (`R_BINDING_CHANGED`).

flow13_table.title: Removal requested by its author
flow13_table.remedy: The listing's author asked from the Astra plugins panel for it to be removed (FLOW-28). From the bound account it is delisted at once: it leaves the catalogue and gets no updates, and installed copies are not removed. For a listing with no bound account the request is held, and a moderator decides it (MOD-9). Only a moderator lists a plugin again; to ask for that, send a report from the panel's report page.

flow13_table.title: Stopped by its author
flow13_table.remedy: A stop was confirmed from this submission's notice link (TRUST-34), so none of its fingerprints publishes. A stop cannot be lifted, and this tag cannot be submitted again (FLOW-26): publish the release under a new tag.

flow13_table.title: Withdrawn before it was checked
flow13_table.remedy: The submission was withdrawn while it was `received` (FLOW-22), so nothing was checked or published. This tag cannot be submitted again (FLOW-26): publish the release under a new tag.

flow13_table.title: Yanked at its author's own request
flow13_table.remedy: The listing's bound account yanked these versions from the Astra plugins panel (FLOW-79). A yank cannot be undone by anyone, and installed copies keep running. A new version is listed as usual.

flow13_table.title: The account holding the binding token is not eligible to bind
flow13_table.remedy: Shown only to the token's owner and to moderators; everyone else sees `B_BINDING_UNUSABLE` (ID-9). The token is sound and the Minice account that holds it is not eligible (DEC-11). The account's own eligibility clears it: once the account is eligible again, a Recheck of the same tag reads it afresh.

flow13_table.title: The binding token cannot be used for this repository
flow13_table.remedy: Shown only to the token's owner and to moderators; everyone else sees `B_BINDING_UNUSABLE` (ID-9). The token on the tagged commit is unknown, revoked, expired or superseded, or was minted for another repository. Mint a fresh token for this repository in the Astra plugins panel, commit its line and push a new tag: the line is read at the attested commit (ID-22), so this tag cannot change.

flow13_table.title: The binding file is not one well-formed binding line
flow13_table.remedy: `.well-known/astra-plugin-owner` must hold exactly one `astra-binding: <token>` line (ID-24). Fix the file and push a new tag: the line is read at the attested commit.

flow13_table.title: The binding token on the tagged commit cannot bind this release
flow13_table.remedy: The token in `.well-known/astra-plugin-owner` at the tagged commit cannot bind this repository (ID-9); the Astra plugins panel tells the token's owner why. Mint a fresh token there if you need one, commit its line and push a new tag.

flow13_table.title: The repository's owner changed since it was bound
flow13_table.remedy: The owner the build attestation names differs from the one this listing's identity record carries (ID-41). A moderator decides what happens next; a new tag or a Recheck does not clear it.

flow13_table.title: The repository was re-created under this name by another owner
flow13_table.remedy: This refusal is permanent for the repository's recorded identity (ID-41): no Recheck, new tag or approval clears it. Only a moderator's identity reset (`M_IDENTITY_RESET`) does, after which the next release is reviewed as a first binding.

flow13_table.title: No binding line where the registry needs one
flow13_table.remedy: From cutover, a first listing and a frozen listing's next release need an `astra-binding:` line in `.well-known/astra-plugin-owner` at the tagged commit (ID-25). Mint a token in the Astra plugins panel, commit its line and push a new tag: the line is read at the attested commit, so this tag cannot change.

flow13_table.title: The bundle is over the size cap
flow13_table.remedy: See `policy/limits.json`. Ship models and datasets as a download the plugin fetches on first run, not inside the bundle.

flow13_table.title: The asset is not named `<id>-<version>-<target>.astraplugin`
flow13_table.remedy: `astra-plugin build` names bundles that way and the reusable release workflow asserts it. A different name is usually one of two real mistakes: a stale bundle left over from the previous version, or one build leg's file uploaded under another leg's name. Neither is caught by the digest, because the digest is taken of whatever was uploaded.

flow13_table.title: The asset could not be fetched
flow13_table.remedy: Re-upload it and comment `/recheck`. If the release is private or the asset was deleted, nothing downstream can run.

flow13_table.title: The asset changed size between the listing and the download
flow13_table.remedy: Do not overwrite a published release asset. Cut a new version instead — a digest that moves is a digest that pins nothing.

flow13_table.title: An asset URL does not belong to the repository being listed
flow13_table.remedy: Every download URL must sit under `https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/download/<tag>/`. This is the one check a user's daemon can make locally that ties the bytes to the repo, so a listing that fails it here would fail there too.

flow13_table.title: The attestation does not verify
flow13_table.remedy: Re-run the release workflow. Do not re-upload the asset by hand — the attestation covers the exact bytes, and hand-uploading is how they stop matching.

flow13_table.title: The bundle has no build attestation
flow13_table.remedy: Build it in GitHub Actions with `actions/attest-build-provenance`, which the Astra reusable release workflow already does. A hand-built bundle is refused however good it is: CI is the only signer, so an author's compromised laptop cannot publish.

flow13_table.title: The attestation was issued to another repository
flow13_table.remedy: The bundle was built somewhere other than the repository being listed. That is exactly the case this check exists to catch.

flow13_table.title: The attestation is for different bytes
flow13_table.remedy: The asset was replaced after CI attested it. Cut a new release; never overwrite an asset in place.

flow13_table.title: The attestation could not be checked — this is not about your release
flow13_table.remedy: Nothing to fix and nothing to rebuild: the verifier could not start. `gh attestation verify` fetches Sigstore's trust root before it can check anything, and when that fetch fails it reports a failure that reads like a bad signature. Run a Recheck — the same bytes usually verify on the next run. It still blocks, because an artifact nobody could verify must not be listed; it blocks as "we could not look", not as "we looked and it was wrong".

flow13_table.title: An entry is an absolute or Windows-style path
flow13_table.remedy: Bundle paths are relative and use `/`. Rebuild with `astra-plugin build` rather than a hand-made zip.

flow13_table.title: An entry name contains `:`
flow13_table.remedy: Rename the file. On Windows `:` opens an NTFS alternate data stream, so the bytes land somewhere nothing looks.

flow13_table.title: An entry name contains a control or invisible character
flow13_table.remedy: Rename the file to printable characters. An entry name is not only a path: it is printed in this report, in the run log and in the job summary, and a newline or a pipe in one forges rows in the table a maintainer reads before approving a listing.

flow13_table.title: Two archive entries share a name
flow13_table.remedy: Rebuild. The second copy would overwrite a file that already matched the manifest, after it was verified.

flow13_table.title: The archive contains a symlink
flow13_table.remedy: Ship the file itself. A symlink's target is not covered by any of the checks its path passes.

flow13_table.title: The archive expands past the extraction cap
flow13_table.remedy: Same cap the daemon enforces. Shrink the payload or fetch it at runtime.

flow13_table.title: Too many files in the archive
flow13_table.remedy: The daemon refuses to extract it, so listing it would publish something uninstallable. See `policy/limits.json`.

flow13_table.title: An entry name ends in a dot or space
flow13_table.remedy: Rename it. Windows strips both silently, so the name in the manifest and the name on disk stop being the same string.

flow13_table.title: An entry contains `..`
flow13_table.remedy: Rebuild. A `..` component is how an archive writes outside the directory it was extracted into.

flow13_table.title: The archive cannot be read
flow13_table.remedy: Rebuild with `astra-plugin build`. A truncated upload is the usual cause.

flow13_table.title: `[capabilities]` names something the daemon has never had
flow13_table.remedy: Use the exact name — `ui_contributions`, not `ui_panels`. An unknown key used to be dropped silently, which is how three shipped examples declared nothing at all.

flow13_table.title: The listing the bot derived does not pass this repository's own validator
flow13_table.remedy: A bug in this registry, not in your plugin. Please leave the issue open.

flow13_table.title: The bytes do not hash to what the attestation covers
flow13_table.remedy: The file at the URL is not the file CI built. Re-run the release workflow; if it happens twice, treat the repository as compromised before you treat it as a bug.

flow13_table.title: `entry.command` is an absolute path
flow13_table.remedy: It must be relative to the install directory, or the name of a declared runtime.

flow13_table.title: `[entry] command` is missing from `plugin.toml`
flow13_table.remedy: Add it.

flow13_table.title: `entry.command` is missing
flow13_table.remedy: Declare the program the daemon should run.

flow13_table.title: `entry.command` is neither a bundled file nor a declared runtime
flow13_table.remedy: Ship the binary in the bundle, or name `python` / `node` / `deno` / `bun`.

flow13_table.title: `entry.command` is a shell
flow13_table.remedy: Run your program directly. A shell as the entry point means the daemon executes whatever `args` say, which is arbitrary code with none of the review the rest of this list applies.

flow13_table.title: `entry.command` escapes the install directory
flow13_table.remedy: Point it at a file inside the bundle.

flow13_table.title: Source in the bundle calls a high-risk host RPC the manifest does not declare
flow13_table.remedy: Declare the capability the call needs, or remove the call. The four that block are `FireTrigger`, `SendChatMessage`, `SetVariable` and `SetThemeContribution` — each of them acts on the user's session rather than inside your plugin.

flow13_table.title: `plugin.id` is not a safe directory name
flow13_table.remedy: Lowercase letters, digits and single hyphens. The id becomes `<plugins_dir>/<id>/` on every user's disk.

flow13_table.title: That id is reserved
flow13_table.remedy: See `policy/reserved-ids.json`. Ids that read as first-party are an impersonation primitive.

flow13_table.title: `plugin.id` is a reserved Windows device name
flow13_table.remedy: Rename. `con`, `prn`, `aux`, `nul`, `com1`-`com9`, `lpt1`-`lpt9` are devices, not directories.

flow13_table.title: That id uses a reserved prefix
flow13_table.remedy: `astra-`, `official-` and `verified-` are first-party only.

flow13_table.title: The source repository is not `owner/name`
flow13_table.remedy: Write it exactly as GitHub does: `you/dice-roller`. No URL, no trailing slash, no branch.

flow13_table.title: The release tag is not a tag
flow13_table.remedy: Copy the tag from the release page — `v0.2.0`, not a commit SHA and not a branch name.

flow13_table.title: `plugin.license` is empty
flow13_table.remedy: Declare an SPDX identifier. A plugin with no licence is code nobody may legally run.

flow13_table.title: That licence is not on the allowlist
flow13_table.remedy: See `policy/spdx-allowlist.json`. It is an allowlist, not a denylist: a licence nobody here has read is one this registry cannot promise anything about. To add one, open a pull request with a sentence on why.

flow13_table.title: The store card's summary is not in English
flow13_table.remedy: Write `plugin.description` in English and put your own language in `locales/<code>.json` under `listing.description`. The card, the search index, every client that predates localization and every user whose language you have not translated all read the English one. This is a SCRIPT check, not a language detector: it refuses a description whose letters are under 60% Latin, and it cannot tell English from French.

flow13_table.title: `en.json`'s `listing.*` disagrees with `plugin.toml`
flow13_table.remedy: `astra-plugin locale sync` rewrites `en.json` from `plugin.toml`. They are the same fact in two files because the manifest crate cannot hold a locale table, and the card is drawn from one while every other language falls back to the other — so a disagreement is a listing that says two things.

flow13_table.title: This release's bundles carry different translations
flow13_table.remedy: Build every platform from the same tree. The store card is derived from one bundle and each platform installs its own, so bundles whose `locales/` differ describe different plugins to different halves of the users.

flow13_table.title: One listing's translations are over the per-listing budget
flow13_table.remedy: See `max_listing_i18n_bytes` in `policy/limits.json`. The catalogue is one signed document every install fetches whole every hour; this budget is what keeps one listing's translations from being everybody's download.

flow13_table.title: A localized card string is over its cap
flow13_table.remedy: See `policy/limits.json`: 64 characters for a name, 4000 for a description. The block is refused, so that language's card falls back to English with nothing explaining why.

flow13_table.title: A locale file declares keys `en.json` does not
flow13_table.remedy: Add them to `en.json` or delete them. `en.json` is the base, so a key that is not in it can never be reached from any other language and is dead weight in every bundle.

flow13_table.title: A locale file is missing keys `en.json` declares
flow13_table.remedy: `astra-plugin locale add <code>` seeds the missing keys from English and leaves what is already translated alone. Every language must carry every key while the daemon falls back per file: a key missing here is not filled in from English, it is shown to the user as a key.

flow13_table.title: A locale file is not a flat map of string to string
flow13_table.remedy: Flatten it. The daemon deserialises `HashMap<String,String>` and drops the WHOLE file on one non-string value — silently, at install time — so a nested object costs every translation in that file and says nothing. Plurals are key suffixes (`msg.done.one`), never nested objects.

flow13_table.title: `locales/` has translations and no `en.json`
flow13_table.remedy: `astra-plugin locale add en`. English is the base every other language falls back to, and the released daemon falls back per FILE rather than per key — it selects one whole locale map and then resolves — so without `en.json` there is nothing to fall back to and the key itself reaches the screen.

flow13_table.title: A locale file is too big to read
flow13_table.remedy: See `max_locale_bytes` and `max_locale_keys` in `policy/limits.json`. The file is refused unread — a locale file is loaded whole by the daemon, by the CLI and by this bot, and before the parse is the only cheap place to stop a runaway one.

flow13_table.title: A locale file is named for a language Astra cannot be set to
flow13_table.remedy: The ten codes are in `AstraPlugins/spec/locales.yaml`. Matching is exact string equality and there are no region tags anywhere in this system — Chinese is `zh`, never `zh-CN` — so a file named anything else is packed, digested, signed, installed, and read by nothing.

flow13_table.title: `MANIFEST.json` is compressed
flow13_table.remedy: It must be stored uncompressed so it can be read without inflating attacker-supplied bytes.

flow13_table.title: The archive holds a file the manifest does not list
flow13_table.remedy: An unlisted file is a file nothing verifies — at install, and at every start afterwards. Rebuild.

flow13_table.title: `plugin.toml` is missing a required field
flow13_table.remedy: `id`, `name` and `version` are all required.

flow13_table.title: A file's content disagrees with the manifest
flow13_table.remedy: Rebuild. If the build is reproducible and this persists, the release asset was tampered with after CI.

flow13_table.title: The archive holds two different `MANIFEST.json`s
flow13_table.remedy: The manifest the central directory points at is not the one at byte zero, and the daemon reads byte zero. This is not something a build tool does by accident.

flow13_table.title: The manifest names a different plugin
flow13_table.remedy: One release, one plugin. A bundle whose manifest names another id installs as that other id.

flow13_table.title: `MANIFEST.json` is malformed
flow13_table.remedy: Rebuild with `astra-plugin build`.

flow13_table.title: `MANIFEST.json` cannot be read from byte zero
flow13_table.remedy: Rebuild with `astra-plugin build`.

flow13_table.title: No `MANIFEST.json` — this is not a v2 bundle
flow13_table.remedy: Rebuild with a current `astra-plugin`.

flow13_table.title: The manifest lists a file the archive does not hold
flow13_table.remedy: Rebuild; the manifest and the archive were produced from different trees.

flow13_table.title: `MANIFEST.json` is not the first archive entry
flow13_table.remedy: The daemon reads it from byte zero. Rebuild rather than repacking by hand.

flow13_table.title: Two artifacts of this release claim the same platform
flow13_table.remedy: Each target gets its own file. Check the build matrix.

flow13_table.title: The manifest's platform has no registry key
flow13_table.remedy: `os`/`arch` must be one of the pairs in `tools/lib/platform.mjs`.

flow13_table.title: A file's size disagrees with the manifest
flow13_table.remedy: Rebuild. The archive was edited after the manifest was written.

flow13_table.title: `MANIFEST.files` is not sorted by path
flow13_table.remedy: Rebuild. The order is part of the format so two builders produce the same bytes.

flow13_table.title: The manifest names a different version
flow13_table.remedy: Retag and rebuild so the tag, the manifest and the filename agree.

flow13_table.title: `plugin.toml` does not say what the plugin is
flow13_table.remedy: Fill in `description` (and `author`). The store card is built entirely out of the bundle — there is no form to type a summary into, by design — so a manifest with no description produces a listing with nothing on it.

flow13_table.title: A metadata field is over its length cap
flow13_table.remedy: See `policy/limits.json`. The store's card has a fixed size; a longer string is truncated somewhere less pleasant.

flow13_table.title: Metadata contains invisible or direction-changing characters
flow13_table.remedy: Remove the zero-width, bidi-override or control characters. They are what makes a card render as a name it does not contain.

flow13_table.title: `min_astra_version` is not a semver version
flow13_table.remedy: Write `"0.9.0"`. A value that does not parse is a requirement that requires nothing.

flow13_table.title: The plugin needs a newer Astra than this registry publishes for
flow13_table.remedy: Lower `min_astra_version`, or wait for that Astra to ship. A listing nobody can install is worse than no listing.

flow13_table.title: The release carries no `.astraplugin` asset
flow13_table.remedy: `astra-plugin build` produces one file per target; attach every one of them to the release. The reusable release workflow does this for you.

flow13_table.title: The repository has not vouched for the account asking
flow13_table.remedy: Commit `.well-known/astra-plugin-owner` on the repository's default branch with your GitHub login on a line of its own, then comment `/recheck`. One commit, no CI: `mkdir -p .well-known && echo YOUR-LOGIN > .well-known/astra-plugin-owner`. That file is the proof this registry asks for: it says somebody who can write to that branch vouches for this login — a proof of write access, not of legal ownership — and it is read live on every run, so deleting a line stops that login opening a new request or passing a `/recheck`. The bot also tries a free shortcut first (`GET /collaborators/{you}/permission`, which grants on `admin` or `maintain`), but GitHub answers that only for a caller that can already see the repository, so for any repository this registry does not itself own it is told nothing at all — a limit of the bot's token, not a finding about you, and not something you can install your way around.

flow13_table.title: `permissions_hash` does not cover the declared permissions
flow13_table.remedy: Rebuild with `astra-plugin build`, which derives the hash from the permissions and cannot emit a mismatch. Astra refuses to install this bundle (§5.3-D, block code PERMISSIONS_HASH_MISMATCH), so listing it would advertise a version nobody can have. The hash is what the consent sheet renders against and what the update gate compares: when it does not cover the permission map, a user can approve one list while the daemon enforces another.

flow13_table.title: Astra ships no daemon for that platform
flow13_table.remedy: `linux-x64`, `windows-x64` and `noarch` are the hosts that exist. macOS and arm64 names are reserved and unusable.

flow13_table.title: The bundle has no `plugin.toml`
flow13_table.remedy: Every plugin carries one; it is what the daemon reads to know what the plugin is. Rebuild with `astra-plugin build`.

flow13_table.title: The manifest probe rejected the bot's own request
flow13_table.remedy: A bug in this registry, not in your plugin. Please leave the issue open.

flow13_table.title: The manifest probe could not be run
flow13_table.remedy: A bug in this registry, not in your plugin. `plugin.toml` was not validated by anything, so the run fails closed.

flow13_table.title: The Release points at a different commit than the one that built it
flow13_table.remedy: `release.target_commitish` and the commit named in the build attestation must be the same. They are not, which means the Release was created against — or re-pointed at — a tree that did not produce these bytes. This matters beyond tidiness: the listing records that commit as the release's provenance, and every relative image in your README is pinned to it, so a mismatch renders pictures from a tree nothing attested. Re-create the Release at the commit the workflow built (`gh release create <tag> --target <sha>`), or re-run the release workflow on the tag.

flow13_table.title: That repository has no release with that tag
flow13_table.remedy: Publish the release (a draft is invisible to everyone but you) and check the tag spelling. The bot reads it unauthenticated, so a private repository looks the same as a missing one.

flow13_table.title: `plugin.toml` and `MANIFEST.json` describe different plugins
flow13_table.remedy: Rebuild from one tree. The daemon installs under the manifest's id and runs what plugin.toml describes.

flow13_table.title: The id or display name claims someone else's mark
flow13_table.remedy: Name it for what it does, not for the service it talks to: `telegram-client` becomes `tg-bridge`, `Spotify Controller` becomes `Music Controller for Spotify` only with the rightsholder's say-so. See `bot/policy/trademarks.json`.

flow13_table.title: This registry has no root-signed trust document yet
flow13_table.remedy: Nothing a submitter can do — the root-key ceremony (SECURITY.md) has not been run, so there is no allowlist to check a workflow against. The bot fails closed rather than accepting a build it cannot place.

flow13_table.title: The id is indistinguishable from a listed plugin
flow13_table.remedy: After NFKC normalisation, case folding, hyphen stripping and confusable folding it is the same string as an existing listing. Two cards a user cannot tell apart cannot both exist. Pick a different name.

flow13_table.title: The release's bundles do not agree on a version
flow13_table.remedy: One release, one version, every target. Check the build matrix.

flow13_table.title: That version is already listed, or is older than one that is
flow13_table.remedy: Releases go forward. Bump the version and cut a new release — a version that is republished with different bytes is how a downgrade attack starts.

flow13_table.title: The build ran a release workflow this registry does not allow
flow13_table.remedy: Call the Astra reusable release workflow and pin it by commit SHA (`uses: mihailinl/AstraPlugins/.github/workflows/plugin-release.yml@<sha>`). Verifying an attestation without pinning which workflow produced it proves only that GitHub built something. The allowed SHAs live in the root-signed `trust.json`; adding one is a root-key ceremony, not a pull request.

flow13_table.title: An appeal was decided
flow13_table.remedy: The outcome, `stands` or `reversed`, is recorded with the moderator's public reason and never the appeal's own text (MOD-32; MOD-33). A `reversed` appeal becomes a new decision; the one appealed stays in the log.

flow13_table.title: A moderator approved this submission
flow13_table.remedy: Nothing to do. An approval clears holds and nothing else: every check runs again in the run that acts on it, and it never shortens a publication delay, a stop or a pending notice (DEC-6).

flow13_table.title: A moderator revoked this repository's binding token
flow13_table.remedy: A moderator revoked the binding token this repository is bound with (ID-17). Listed versions are not touched. Nothing clears this code: the next release is refused `B_BINDING_UNUSABLE` (§7.2), and that code says what clears it.

flow13_table.title: A moderator delisted this plugin
flow13_table.remedy: The plugin leaves the catalogue and gets no updates, and installed copies keep running (§7.2). A new release does not list it again. You can appeal from the Astra plugins panel (MOD-31); only a moderator's relist (`M_RELIST`) brings it back.

flow13_table.title: A moderator deprecated these versions
flow13_table.remedy: A moderator published an advisory with action `warn` for these versions (§7.2). They stay listed and installable: Astra badges them and tells the user, and blocks and stops nothing. The advisory stands until a moderator lifts it (`M_UNREVOKE`). You can appeal from the Astra plugins panel (MOD-31).

flow13_table.title: A moderator reset this listing's recorded identity
flow13_table.remedy: A moderator voided every identity this plugin id had recorded, and deleted its identity record where it had one (§7.2; ID-40). Like every reversal, it was held and confirmed by the registry's operator before it applied (MOD-9). It clears `B_REPOSITORY_RECYCLED` for the identities it voided, and nothing clears it. The listing is now frozen: its next release needs a binding line, and is held for a moderator as a first binding.

flow13_table.title: A moderator rejected this submission
flow13_table.remedy: A Recheck does not reopen a rejection (FLOW-18). You can appeal it from the Astra plugins panel; if a moderator reverses the rejection on appeal, exactly one Recheck of this submission is opened (MOD-33).

flow13_table.title: A moderator listed this plugin again
flow13_table.remedy: A moderator lifted the plugin's delisting (§7.2). Like every reversal, it was held and confirmed by the registry's operator before it applied (MOD-9). The plugin is back in the catalogue and gets updates again. Nothing to do.

flow13_table.title: A moderator revoked these versions
flow13_table.remedy: A moderator published an advisory for these versions (§7.2). With action `block_install`, Astra refuses new installs and updates and leaves a running copy alone; with `disable`, it also stops installed copies, and they do not start again. The advisory stands until a moderator lifts it (`M_UNREVOKE`). You can appeal from the Astra plugins panel (MOD-31).

flow13_table.title: A moderator lifted an advisory
flow13_table.remedy: A moderator deleted the advisory that deprecated or revoked these versions (§7.2). Like every reversal, it was held and confirmed by the registry's operator before it applied (MOD-9). Its effect lifts on each machine at the withdrawal list's next higher serial. Nothing to do.

flow13_table.title: A moderator yanked these versions
flow13_table.remedy: These versions leave the catalogue and are no longer offered, and installed copies keep running (§7.2). A yank cannot be undone by anyone (B.3): an appeal is recorded, but no decision brings these versions back (MOD-10). A later release is judged like any other.

flow13_table.title: The RPC scan read source files only
flow13_table.remedy: Compiled binaries and vendored SDK code are not decidable by string matching. This check catches accidents; it does not catch anyone who is trying.

flow13_table.title: The English card rule was waived for this repository
flow13_table.remedy: Nothing to do. The waiver is a reviewed entry in `policy/listing-language-exemptions.json`, keyed on the repository rather than on the plugin id so that a rename cannot walk past it.

flow13_table.title: The approval named a different submission from this one
flow13_table.remedy: Nothing published and nothing was lost. An `/approve` carries the fingerprint printed in the comment it answers, and this run's fingerprint is different — the repository, the tag, the version or the release assets changed after that comment was written. Read the table above as it stands now and, if it is still a yes, copy the `/approve` line out of **this** comment. An approval has to be about something a person actually read.

flow13_table.title: A maintainer cleared the hold
flow13_table.remedy: Nothing to do. The hold is gone; every check above was re-run from scratch in this run, against the release as it is today, and what publishes is what this run verified.

flow13_table.title: A maintainer waived part of the publication delay
flow13_table.remedy: Nothing to do, but the shortened window is on the record: somebody with write access to this registry edited `publish_after` in the queue entry, and the commit that did it says who and when. Every check still ran from scratch against today's bytes.

flow13_table.title: The release assets changed during the delay, so the clock restarted
flow13_table.remedy: Do not overwrite a published release asset. The delay is a delay on *these bytes*; replacing them mid-window starts it again, which is the only thing that stops a swap timed for the end of the window.

flow13_table.title: The publication delay has elapsed
flow13_table.remedy: Nothing to do. Every check was re-run from scratch just now, against the bytes as they are today.

flow13_table.title: Held for the publication delay because the plugin holds a high-risk permission
flow13_table.remedy: Nothing to do. Every auto-published release of a plugin holding any high-risk permission waits, whether or not this release changed anything — §5.5's realistic takeover case is a malicious version with *identical* permissions, and a delay that only fired on changes would never fire on it.

flow13_table.title: Waiting out the publication delay
flow13_table.remedy: Nothing to do. It publishes itself at the time stated above without anybody touching it.

flow13_table.title: A maintainer published this without waiting
flow13_table.remedy: Nothing to do, and the shortened window is on the record. Somebody with write access to this registry typed `/publish` against these exact bytes, which is the same act as editing `publish_after` by hand and needs the same access — but every check in the comment above it ran again from scratch first, which a hand-written listing would not have.

flow13_table.title: Held for the publication delay because the permission set grew
flow13_table.remedy: Nothing to do. A widening inside the non-high-risk set publishes itself after the delay; the delay exists so the author hears about it first.

flow13_table.title: Approved, and published without waiting
flow13_table.remedy: Nothing to do. A first listing has no installed copies, so the publication delay would have protected nobody who had not already chosen to install it — and a person read this submission, which is the check the delay stands in for. The delay still applies to every later release from this repository, where existing installs follow an update whether or not anybody looked.

flow13_table.title: Not published: the registry's operator withheld this exact build
flow13_table.remedy: An operator deny record on `main` names this fingerprint (TRUST-33). No Recheck, approval or moderator decision clears it; only the operator removing the record does. A new tag is a new fingerprint and is judged afresh.

flow13_table.title: Published, with nobody in the loop
flow13_table.remedy: Nothing to do. This is what a routine release is supposed to look like.

flow13_table.title: Not published, because a check failed
flow13_table.remedy: Fix the blocking findings above and comment `/recheck`. The policy did not reject this; a check did.

flow13_table.title: What happens next, and by when
flow13_table.remedy: See docs/POLICY.md. If this passes the stated deadline, say so on this issue — a missed SLA is a bug in the policy, not in your release.

flow13_table.title: Shorter delay: this author has a clean release history here
flow13_table.remedy: Nothing to do.

flow13_table.title: The manifest declares a permission this registry has no name for
flow13_table.remedy: Check the spelling against POLICY.md's permission table. An unknown key grants nothing — the daemon default-denies — so it is reported rather than blocked, but a permission nobody can name is also a permission no consent sheet can describe.

flow13_table.title: The binding token changed since this listing was bound
flow13_table.remedy: The `astra-binding:` line at the tagged commit carries a different token from the one this listing's identity record holds (ID-41 row 6). The account that held the previous binding is told, and a moderator's approval publishes it only once the author objection window has passed since that account was told, or since its binding was revoked (ID-60; ID-61).

flow13_table.title: A check handed the decision to a person
flow13_table.remedy: Not a rejection and not one of the three policy events — a near-miss name or a display-name collision that the bot is not entitled to rule on. Same 48-hour SLA.

flow13_table.title: The display name matches a listed plugin's, bar case, spacing or lookalike letters
flow13_table.remedy: Held for a human. The store shows names, not ids, so two identical names are two identical cards. A byte-identical name counts: it is the strongest form of the collision, not an exception to it.

flow13_table.title: The display name mixes alphabets
flow13_table.remedy: Held for a human. Write the name in one alphabet. A name that borrows a single Cyrillic or Greek letter for its Latin shape renders as a name it does not contain, and the id charset cannot catch it because the id is not the string on the card.

flow13_table.title: First binding line on a published listing — a moderator approves it once
flow13_table.remedy: This listing was published before it had an identity record, and this release is the first to carry an `astra-binding:` line (MIG-10). A moderator approves it once; the approval then waits the operator's objection window like every approval (DEC-6). Once a release under this binding is published, later releases are not held for this again.

flow13_table.title: First listing — a person reads it, once, ever
flow13_table.remedy: Nothing to do but wait. This is one of exactly three events that block on a human, and it happens once per plugin: every later release from the same repository is zero-touch.

flow13_table.title: One of the four acting-outside-the-plugin RPCs is named inside a `generated/` or `vendor/` directory
flow13_table.remedy: Held for a human. Those two directory names are chosen by whoever built the bundle, not by a toolchain, so the scan no longer skips them — but a real generated tree is a normal thing to ship. Declare the capability or permission if the call is yours, or say in the issue what wrote the file.

flow13_table.title: The repository this plugin is listed from changed
flow13_table.remedy: Say in the issue what happened — a rename, a transfer, a fork taking over maintenance. Every installed copy carries a pin to the old repository, so this is an author change until somebody says otherwise.

flow13_table.title: The release asks for a high-risk permission it did not have before
flow13_table.remedy: Say in the issue what the new permission is for, in one sentence a user would accept. The four that block are `client`, `dom_access`, `send_chat_message` and `set_theme_contribution`; each reaches outside the plugin's own surface.

flow13_table.title: The id is one edit away from a listed plugin
flow13_table.remedy: Held for a human, not rejected — plenty of honest names are near-misses. If it is deliberate, say so in the issue and it will be approved faster.

flow13_table.title: Two entries differ only in letter case
flow13_table.remedy: Rename one. Linux keeps both; Windows and macOS keep one, and the daemon refuses the bundle there — so this lists cleanly and then fails to install for most of your users.

flow13_table.title: The bundle runs a different command than `plugin.toml` declares
flow13_table.remedy: The daemon executes the manifest's. Usually a stale `plugin.toml`.

flow13_table.title: A compiled file contains a host RPC name
flow13_table.remedy: Not blocking, and usually not a call: a linked SDK client contains the name of every method on the service whether or not you invoke it. Named so it is on the record, not because it is evidence.

flow13_table.title: A non-blocking host RPC is named inside a `generated/` or `vendor/` directory
flow13_table.remedy: Recorded. Declare the capability if the call is yours.

flow13_table.title: Source in the bundle names a host RPC the manifest does not declare
flow13_table.remedy: Not blocking. Declare the capability if the call is real; ignore this if the string is a comment or a log line.

flow13_table.title: The bundle carries a legacy in-ZIP `SIGNATURE`/`PUBKEY`
flow13_table.remedy: Harmless and ignored. It is never a trust signal here — trust comes from the attestation and from this registry's countersignature. `astra-plugin build` stops writing it.

flow13_table.title: The plugin's name is mostly outside the Latin script
flow13_table.remedy: Nothing to fix, necessarily — a product name is not prose and is legitimately anything. The summary beside it is held to English, so check that the two read as one listing.

flow13_table.title: `en.json` declares neither reserved listing key
flow13_table.remedy: `astra-plugin locale sync` writes `listing.name` and `listing.description`. They are the only two keys the registry reads out of `locales/`, so without them a plugin that translates its whole interface still gets an English-only store card.

flow13_table.title: A translation describes English that has since been rewritten
flow13_table.remedy: `astra-plugin locale sync` before the next release. The affected strings fall back to English on the card rather than being shown: a confidently wrong sentence in a language nobody here can proof-read is worse than a correct one in the wrong language, and the release is not refused over prose.

flow13_table.title: A file's recorded mode differs from the archive's
flow13_table.remedy: The daemon applies the manifest's mode and refuses the mismatch, so this lists and then does not install. Rebuild.

flow13_table.title: Awaiting an operator acknowledgement
flow13_table.remedy: The registry changed its bot, and until an operator acknowledges that change the plugins service holds the bot's calls (TRUST-45). Nothing about this submission has been decided and nothing is lost; it continues once the change is acknowledged, with nothing for you to do.
